name: AI policy topics
description: Policies written in plain language for an AI provider to evaluate, for the cases no word list can reach -- implication, tone, novel slang, and languages the term lists do not cover. Topic rules are advisory and can never auto-action. Every topic carries counter-examples, because the failure mode of an AI reviewer is confident over-flagging, and the counter-examples are what hold it back.

rules.prompt: Hate speech: content that attacks, dehumanises or calls for harm against people because of race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation or disability. Self-description and reclaimed language by members of the group in question are NOT hate speech.
examples: our kind only, no outsiders in this group
they're animals and everyone knows it, look at the statistics
anyone from that country is a thief, change my mind
I don't hate them I just think they shouldn't be allowed near children
counterExamples: black and proud, she/her, BLM
I'm a disabled trans woman and I mod for a living
queer artist, commissions open
I write about the history of racial violence in America
got called a slur in the last instance, staff please look at the logs
as a Jewish player I'd rather not be in worlds with Nazi avatars
rules.note: The hardest distinction for a model to make is between a person using a word about themselves and a person using it about someone else. The counter-examples are all the first kind and the model should return no match for any of them. If this topic starts flagging self-description, it is miscalibrated and should be disabled until it is fixed.

rules.prompt: Political statements: partisan advocacy, campaign slogans, election claims, or statements taking a side on a contested political issue. Merely mentioning that politics exists, or stating a personal identity that is politically contested, is not a political statement.
examples: vote them out in November, our country depends on it
the election was stolen and everyone knows it
proud member of the resistance, no fascists in my DMs
one nation under God, back the blue, 2A absolutist
counterExamples: poli sci major, ask me about voting systems
I'm an immigrant and I love it here
trans rights are human rights
no politics in this group please, I come here to relax
history teacher, I cover the Cold War
rules.note: 'Trans rights are human rights' sits in the counter-examples on purpose and groups will disagree about it. The reasoning: a statement that a category of member deserves to exist is an identity statement, not a campaign position, and treating it as partisan tells those members they are a controversy. A group that disagrees should say so in its own policy rather than editing this prompt to be vaguer.

rules.prompt: Sexual content in a space that includes minors: explicit description, solicitation, innuendo, kink vocabulary, or links to adult material. Stating a sexual orientation or gender identity is not sexual content.
examples: dm me if you want to have some fun, 18+ only, my linktree has everything
switch looking for a dom, be patient with me
check my bio link for uncensored stuff
let's go somewhere private and I'll show you
counterExamples: gay and taken, he/him
married 6 years, we play together
I run a sex education Discord for over-18s, not recruiting here
asexual, please don't flirt with me
minors DNI on my other account, this one is clean
rules.note: For all-ages and family-friendly groups. The last counter-example is the one to watch: an account saying 'minors DNI' is behaving responsibly, and a model that reads the phrase as an adult-content marker will flag exactly the people who are being careful. Use the 18+ variant of this topic in adult venues instead.

rules.prompt: In a venue where adult content is permitted, flag only sexual content that is non-consensual, involves incapacitation, depicts real animals, is commercial solicitation, or is pushed into a display name or status where other members cannot avoid seeing it. Ordinary explicit description in a bio is NOT a match.
examples: I don't ask about consent, I take what I want
into girls who are too drunk to say no
rates in my bio, cashapp for the good stuff, meet ups possible
display name: CumDumpsterForHire
counterExamples: switch, into rope and praise, limits in my carrd, always negotiate first
CNC is my thing, safeword is red, I will ask you three times
sex worker, this account is personal, I don't advertise here
explicit ERP in private instances with friends only, 21+
rules.note: The counter-examples are all explicit and all fine -- that is the point of an adult venue. What separates them from the examples is consent, negotiation and placement. A model that flags the counter-examples has been given the all-ages policy by mistake; check which topic is enabled.

rules.prompt: Content sexualising minors: sexual interest in children or in child-coded characters, soliciting minors, normalising adult-child contact, or advertising sexual content involving under-18s. Do not match anti-abuse statements, survivor disclosure, or safeguarding discussion.
examples: age is just a number if you're mature enough, dm me
I prefer them young and inexperienced, hmu privately
attracted to minors but I'd never act on it, looking for others who understand
selling content, no age restrictions, don't ask questions
counterExamples: pedos DNI, I will report you
survivor of CSA, I mod for a youth support server
I'm 15, please don't add me if you're an adult
my fursona is a cub character but this account is strictly SFW and I'm 24
I research online grooming patterns for a child safety NGO
rules.note: The single most consequential topic in this list, in both directions -- a missed match is a child harmed, and a false match is an accusation that can destroy someone's life and is almost impossible to walk back. Note the third counter-example: a minor stating their own age is a safeguarding matter handled by the underage-risk list, not an instance of sexualisation, and must not be flagged here. Never action a match from this topic alone; a topic rule is advisory by design and this is the topic where that matters most.

rules.prompt: Signals that the account holder is under 18: a stated age or birth year, school year references, or unambiguous life-stage context. Do not match adults reminiscing about school, teachers describing pupils, or protective 'minors DNI' markers written by adults.
examples: 14, she/her, I love drawing and my cat
8th grade, add me, I'm on after homework
born 2012, don't be weird
can't voice chat, my mum is asleep and I have school tomorrow
counterExamples: 27, I teach 8th grade science
haven't felt this way since high school
minors DNI, I'm 30 and this account is 18+
college freshman, 19
my daughter plays too, she's 12, I supervise
rules.note: A match here is not misconduct. In an 18+ venue it is a safeguarding obligation and in an all-ages venue it is just useful context. Frame any conversation accordingly -- a teenager who lied about their age to get into an adult world has usually been told to by someone else, and the sensible first question is who.

rules.prompt: Harassment and threats aimed at a specific person: threats of violence, suicide baiting, sustained abuse, or publishing someone's private information. Competitive trash talk about a game is not harassment.
examples: I know what city you live in and I have screenshots
kill yourself, nobody would notice
everyone block @user, here's their real name and workplace
I'll be in every instance you join until you quit
counterExamples: I will absolutely destroy you at Rec Room paintball
get rekt, rematch tomorrow
someone DMed me a death threat, screenshots attached, who do I send this to
I block people fast, nothing personal
my ex is in this community, I'd rather not be in the same instance
rules.note: The third counter-example is a victim reporting a threat, and it contains the threat verbatim -- a model reading only for keywords will flag the person asking for help. That is the specific failure this topic's counter-examples exist to prevent. Check who is speaking before you act on any match here.

rules.prompt: Violent extremism: affiliation with or glorification of terrorist and violent extremist movements, praise for mass attackers, or calls for political or racial violence. Academic, historical, journalistic and counter-extremism discussion is not a match, and neither is ordinary religious observance.
examples: the saint knew what had to be done, read the manifesto
accelerate, the system falls either way, get ready
proud member, our day is coming, 1488
he had the right idea, just bad execution
counterExamples: Muslim, prayers five times a day, inshallah
I research radicalisation pathways for a university
Heathen, I wear a Mjolnir and I am not a Nazi before you ask
history channel, I make videos about WW2 tank design
my grandfather survived the camps
rules.note: Two specific miscalibrations to watch for. First, ordinary Muslim devotional language is not extremism and a model that flags 'inshallah' is doing Islamophobia with extra steps. Second, Norse pagans have spent twenty years being mistaken for neo-Nazis because both use the same runes -- the third counter-example is written the way real Heathen bios are written, pre-emptively defensive, and it must not match.

rules.prompt: Anti-LGBTQ+ content: slurs, denial that trans people are the gender they say they are, framing LGBTQ+ people as predators or as mentally ill, or advocating conversion therapy. Members describing their own identity, using reclaimed words about themselves, or stating any pronouns at all are never a match.
examples: there are two genders and no amount of surgery changes that
keep them away from kids, that's all I'll say
it's a mental illness and we used to treat it
I'll use whatever pronouns I feel like, cope
counterExamples: trans woman, she/her, HRT 3 years
certified dyke, my wife thinks it's funny
xe/xem, please try, I know it's new
it/its, yes really, thank you for asking
gender critical friends have blocked me, I'm fine with that
questioning, please be patient with me
rules.note: Read counter-examples three and four carefully. Neopronouns and it/its pronouns are real pronoun sets that real people use, and a model trained to associate unusual pronouns with trolling will flag the most vulnerable members in the group. No match may ever be returned for a pronoun field. Counter-example two is a reclaimed slur used self-referentially and is also not a match.

rules.prompt: Advertising and solicitation: promoting another server or community, selling goods or services, asking for money, or driving traffic off-platform. A creator mentioning their work without a sales pitch is not advertising.
examples: join my server, we're better than this one and we pay staff
avatars from $40, dm for the catalogue, payment upfront
invest with me, guaranteed 10% weekly, ask how
follow, sub, and hit the bell for daily VRChat content
counterExamples: I make avatars, this is my personal account
artist, portfolio in bio
I stream sometimes, no pressure
looking for a group to play with, not recruiting for anything
rules.note: Set to note because most groups tolerate some promotion and many exist for it. The line the prompt draws is between mentioning and pitching. In a creative community, raise the threshold or disable this -- VRChat's economy runs on commissions and a group that flags every artist will lose its artists.

rules.prompt: Scams and phishing: fake giveaways, impersonating platform or group staff, credential harvesting, fraudulent investment or recovery services, or pressure to move a conversation somewhere unmoderated to complete a transaction.
examples: VRChat staff here, your account is flagged, verify at this link
free Nitro for the first 50, click fast
I can recover your stolen crypto, 20% fee, proof in my DMs
I accidentally reported you, talk to this Steam admin to clear it
counterExamples: group moderator, my staff role is listed on the group page
I got scammed last week, here's what the message looked like so you don't fall for it
I do actual freelance security work, references available
giving away three avatar commissions to celebrate 1k, comment below
rules.note: Counter-example two is a member warning others and quoting the scam in full, which keyword matching flags every time. A model should read intent. Also note that scam content often appears on compromised long-standing accounts -- if the flagged member has two years of good history, consider a password conversation before a ban.

rules.prompt: Self-harm and suicide risk in the account holder: statements of intent, goodbye messages, describing a plan or means, or expressing that others would be better off without them. This is a welfare signal, not a rule violation.
examples: won't be around much longer, thanks for everything
I have a plan and a date, don't try to talk me out of it
relapsed again, deeper this time
nobody would notice if I just stopped logging in
counterExamples: recovered, 2 years clean, happy to talk to anyone struggling
depression sucks but I'm managing, therapy helps
suicide prevention volunteer, ask me for resources
this game saved my life honestly
I'm dead tired, going to sleep
rules.note: Never treat a match here as misconduct, and never action it automatically -- the correct response is a person reaching out with support resources, and possibly nothing else at all. Counter-example one is someone in recovery offering to help others, which a naive classifier reads as risk; flagging them for their own recovery would be actively harmful. Groups without anyone trained to respond should think hard before enabling this rather than enabling it and letting flags sit unread.

rules.prompt: Impersonation: claiming to be platform staff, group staff, a verified account, or a specific real person, when the account is not. Fan accounts and parody accounts that clearly label themselves are not impersonation.
examples: VRChat Moderation Team - Official
group admin (unofficial but basically staff)
verified ✓ developer account
this is my real account, the other one is the fake
counterExamples: parody account, not the real person, obviously
fan account, I just really like their music
actual group staff, check the group roster
my main got compromised, this is the backup, staff can verify
rules.note: Impersonating staff is how most social-engineering attacks in VRChat begin, which is why it is worth catching. Verify against the group roster before acting -- the fourth counter-example is a real member in a bad situation, and treating them as an impersonator compounds it.

rules.prompt: Drug sales or supply: offering to sell, source or ship controlled substances. Recovery discussion, harm-reduction information, references to legal cannabis where the member lives, and mentions of prescribed medication are not matches.
examples: carts and edibles, shipping nationwide, telegram in bio
got pressies and tabs, dm for menu
plug for the whole east coast, don't ask twice
counterExamples: 6 months sober, one day at a time
420 friendly, legal where I live
harm reduction volunteer, I carry naloxone
on ADHD meds, please be patient if I ramble
we do not allow drug talk in this group, that's the rule
rules.note: The distinction is supply, not use. Flagging members for being in recovery, for taking prescribed medication, or for legal cannabis use would be intrusive and pointless -- all four appear in the counter-examples. Set to review because the sales cases are usually obvious once a human reads them.

rules.prompt: Gore and shock content: linking to or advertising real-world death, injury or animal cruelty footage, or describing it in detail to disturb people. Horror fiction, special-effects work, medical and veterinary content, and true-crime discussion are not matches.
examples: got the full uncensored version, dm for the link
collection of real execution footage, ask nicely
I'll describe it in detail if you want, watch you flinch
counterExamples: horror SFX artist, my portfolio is not for the squeamish
vet nurse, my photos are clinical
true crime podcast host
I make Silent Hill avatars
rules.note: Real footage of real people is the line. Everything in the counter-examples is fictional, clinical or journalistic and should not match. In a horror-themed community this topic will need watching or disabling.
